⣾⣽⣻⢿⡿⣟⣯⣷⣾telem: every session, event and log, from the browser to the server to a file FLYBYME/surfdns#62
Open • FLYBYME (Tim) opened about 1 minute ago • 0 comments


                                                                              
  │ full logging like dmesg or whatever. like a kernel. every session needs to
  │ be tracked.                                                               
  │ i would like a ui viewable centralized distributed logging system that is 
  │ configurable.                                                             
                                                                              
  Nothing that happens in a browser is visible to the platform. A part throws,
  a call fails, a page                                                        
  never finishes booting — and the only record is a console the person had to 
  have open. Meanwhile                                                        
  the server's own logs are good ( [builder] released chrome@0.2.6 from HEAD  
  (200b32c) ) and reachable                                                   
  only by  journalctl  on the box.                                            
                                                                              
  ## What to build                                                            
                                                                              
  A  telem  Extension, in mesh-core, plus whatever server side it needs in    
  mesh-                                                                       
  serve.                                                                      
                                                                              
  It collects, from the page:                                                 
                                                                              
  • every log the kernel already buffers ( createLogBuffer  in mesh-web — it  
  exists and nothing                                                          
  ships it anywhere)                                                          
  • every contract call: key, duration, outcome, and the error kind when it   
  fails                                                                       
  • boot: which parts mounted, in what order, how long each took, and which   
  did not                                                                     
  • unhandled errors and rejections                                           
  • the session: a stable id per page load, so a person's whole visit is one  
  thread                                                                      
                                                                              
  It ships them up, batched. Note the transport constraint before designing:  
  the API speaks HTTP                                                         
  and SSE, and SSE is one-way down. There is no browser WebSocket — that is   
  deliberate                                                                  
  ( api/methods/stream.ts:4 ). So this is a batched POST with a flush on      
  visibilitychange , and it                                                   
  must never lose the last batch when a tab closes.                           
                                                                              
  Server side it needs to reach a collection and a file. The collection is    
  what a UI reads; the                                                        
  file is what survives a database being unavailable, which is exactly when   
  logs matter most.                                                           
                                                                              
  ## Configurable, and this is the part to get right                          
                                                                              
  A logger nobody can turn down is a logger somebody turns off. Levels, and   
  which categories ship at                                                    
  all, must be settable per site, from the site record — not a constant, not  
  an environment                                                              
  variable on one node. Sampling for the noisy ones.                          
                                                                              
  Default to something a person would accept: errors and boot always, calls   
  sampled, debug off.                                                         
                                                                              
  ## What to be careful about                                                 
                                                                              
  • This is a privacy surface. It sends what people do to a server that keeps 
  it. Never send                                                              
  ticket values, passwords, or the contents of form fields — call keys and    
  outcomes, not inputs.                                                       
  Say in your plan comment what you decided to send and what you deliberately 
  do not.                                                                     
  • It must not be able to break a page. A telemetry extension that throws, or
  that blocks boot                                                            
  waiting on a POST, is worse than no telemetry. Fail closed and silent.      
  • Volume. Every call from every page of every site, unbounded, is a way to  
  fill a disk.                                                                
                                                                              
  ## Scope                                                                    
                                                                              
  Build the pipe and the storage and make it configurable. A UI for reading it
  is the next issue —                                                         
  but make sure what you store can actually be queried by session, by site, by
  level and by time,                                                          
  because a log nobody can filter is a file.                                  


View this issue on GitHub: https://github.com/FLYBYME/surfdns/issues/62
